source_title: Chipotle Mexican Grill, Inc. Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2015 Results; CDC Investigation Over; Chipotle Welcomes Customers Back to Restaurants
publisher_issuer: Chipotle Mexican Grill, Inc. (press release / Form 8-K exhibit, Business Wire)
company_context: Chipotle Mexican Grill is a U.S. fast-casual restaurant chain. In late 2015 it was hit by E. coli O26 outbreaks (CDC reported 55 sickened across 11 states in the larger outbreak) plus related foodborne-illness publicity, sharply denting traffic and sales before the CDC declared the investigation over in early 2016.
evidence_summary: Q4 2015 revenue was $997.5 million, a 6.8% decrease versus Q4 2014, driven primarily by a 14.6% decrease in comparable restaurant sales attributed to publicity around foodborne-illness incidents. The company opened 79 restaurants in the quarter (229 for the year), reaching 2,010 total restaurants. Full-year 2015 revenue was $4.5 billion, up 9.6% (driven by new restaurants not yet in the comparable base). The release announced that the CDC concluded its E. coli investigation, and the company rolled out an enhanced food-safety program (reported elsewhere at ~$25 million) to rebuild trust.
outcome_evidence: Q4 2015 comparable sales fell 14.6% on foodborne-illness publicity; CDC concluded its investigation and Chipotle announced it could move forward with an enhanced food-safety plan. Outcome sequence: 18 (quality/trust failure) then 13 (temporary shock with recovery), as comparable sales recovered in subsequent years.
source_limitations: Both the Business Wire release and the SEC EDGAR 8-K exhibit returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; figures are quoted verbatim from search snippets of the official Business Wire/IR release and corroborated by the CDC archive page and contemporaneous reporting. Full multi-year recovery trajectory is from later filings, not this single release.
directly_stated: Q4 2015 comparable restaurant sales down 14.6% due to foodborne-illness publicity
2,010 total restaurants; 79 opened in Q4, 229 in FY2015
CDC concluded its E. coli investigation
inferred: demand shock was trust-driven, not pricing or demand-generation driven
investment in food safety was a corrective good action enabling later recovery
why_useful_for_opsiq: Clean quality/trust shock with a quantified comparable-sales collapse followed by documented recovery. Tests OpsIQ's ability to classify a temporary trust shock (13) distinct from structural demand collapse (14), and to credit corrective food-safety action in re-evaluation.
